The PKGBUILD file defines a standard font package for Arch Linux, sourcing the font file and its license from the official Google Fonts GitHub repository at a fixed commit hash. The checksums (sha256sums) are provided and match the expected values for the specified files, ensuring integrity.

The package function installs the font and license to the appropriate system directories using standard install commands. No network operations, file manipulations, or system modifications occur during the package() phase beyond copying the pre-downloaded and verified files. The use of a fixed commit ensures reproducibility, and the operations are consistent with typical AUR font packaging practices.

There are no signs of obfuscated code, unexpected downloads, data exfiltration, or execution of external scripts. The package serves only to install a font and its license, with no runtime components or post-install hooks. All actions are transparent and aligned with the declared purpose.

<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The .SRCINFO file for ttf-quintessential declares two sources: a TrueType font file (Quintessential-Regular.ttf) and its corresponding license (OFL.txt), both fetched over HTTPS from the official Google Fonts GitHub repository using a pinned commit hash (883939708704a19a295e0652036369d22469e8dc). This ensures reproducible builds and prevents tampering via mutable branches.

The SHA-256 checksums are provided for both files and match their expected values, confirming integrity. The package is a standard font package with no build-time scripts or executable code. The license is appropriately set to a custom SIL Open Font License, and conflicts are correctly declared with similar font packages to prevent file collisions.

All sources are from the project's legitimate upstream (Google Fonts) over secure channels, and no network activity, file operations, or commands outside standard packaging norms are present in this metadata file. There is no evidence of obfuscation, unauthorized downloads, or malicious behavior.
</details>
